newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa building sector emerges from trough - IBCA.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa building sector emerges from trough - IBCA.

text.p: South Africa's construction industry has emerged healthier from tough times in the early 1990s and is poised to benefit from an expected upturn, a report from European credit rating agency IBCA said on Tuesday.

The industry has suffered heavily over recent years as the sector stagnated and many construction firms were forced to embark on radical restructuring programmes. But IBCA said most companies had now emerged leaner and fitter.

"Most of the groups in the industry are...well positioned to benefit if the expected improved conditions materialise, and similarly better able to withstand adverse market conditions," the report said.
It added available data so far showed investment in real terms in the industry was set to grow three percent in 1996, after five years of slump. In 1994 and 1995 the figure was a drop of one percent.

IBCA said government funds for infrastructural development were now beginning to come through and should boost the sector in the short-term after being tied up due to bottlenecks in the delivery system.
South African building firms are also starting to spread their wings overseas.
"Other growth opportunities are being explored in Africa and to a lesser extent in the newly industrialised countries of Asia and the Middle East," the report said.
But IBCA said recent unexpected losses or drops in earnings from companies like Group Five showed the construction industry was still volatile and carried high risks.

"Major unanticipated losses or drops in earnings during the most recent financial year by some companies indicate the inherent volatility and high business risk associated with the industry," IBCA said.
"Nonetheless, the general trend has been one of gradually strengthening balance sheets and modest improvements in profitability," the agency added.
